doc.title: Ray Blue interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 23, 2022

title: Studying improvisation with Sonny Sharrock
summary: Blue studied improv with guitarist Sonny Sharrock, who introduced the jazz schools of Trane, Miles, Monk and Ornette.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Yeah. It’s what they do, how they do, what they do. I’ll put it like that. It’s what they do, how they do it and with what they do. And it just woof — yeah. Sonny Sharrock taught me about that kind of thing. I studied with Sonny, a guitarist.

Sonny taught me about it. I studied, I did some improv study with Sonny. And Sonny introduced me to five schools of jazz: Trane, Miles, Monk, Ornette, and — Monk, Miles, Trane, Ornette and who’s the fifth one? Well those four.

Yeah. And the thing was to get inside of that — you learn so much you know, you take compositions from any and all of them and you learn them and you analyze them. You learn the language that they’re using, and how they’re using harmonies you know. How they’re presenting their lines, the melody lines and their phrases. You listen to the records and how they’re interpreted on the recordings you know. Yeah. I still miss Sonny. I still miss Sonny.
He wasn’t on the scene all that long, was he?
No, I would say he was kind of young when he passed, man. Sonny was only 52, 53 when he passed. You know he’d done work with Miles and with Herbie Mann and a bunch of others. Pharoah.
